description: The plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several variants of large language models, including a baseline “Vanilla” model and multiple configurations of the proposed “SepLLM” and “StrmLLM” architectures, as evaluated in the paper “SepLLM: Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.” The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 0 to 140,000 with major tick marks at intervals of 20,000, and uses a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 with tick marks at 0.1 intervals, also on a linear scale. The “Vanilla” model (purple line with circle markers) starts at approximately 3.4 and steadily decreases to around 2.75 by 140,000 iterations. The “StrmLLM (n=64)” (blue line with square markers) begins near 3.4, drops sharply to about 2.9 by 20,000 iterations, then plateaus slightly above 2.9. The “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (orange line with triangle markers) starts at 3.4, declines to ~2.8 by 40,000 iterations, and stabilizes near 2.78. The “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (green line with diamond markers) follows a similar trajectory to the H variant but converges slightly lower, around 2.77. The “SepLLM (n=64)” (red line with cross markers) begins at 3.4, drops to ~2.8 by 40,000, and settles near 2.76. The “SepLLM (n=128)” (dark blue line with plus markers) starts at 3.4, decreases to ~2.85 by 20,000, and converges near 2.79. All models show a rapid initial loss reduction followed by slower convergence, with the SepLLM variants generally achieving lower final loss than Vanilla and StrmLLM.
